title: Use a network diagram to show who sent what to whom.
rule: Pick the senders by one rule read the same way for every side, and draw every sender the rule finds, folded into one bar for each side where the question asks about the side. Draw each sender and each receiver as a solid bar as tall as its amount, with its name and amount beside it, and join them with links in a light fill with a thin edge in the bars’ ink, each as wide as its amount, in one linear unit for the whole drawing, with a key of widths (Rule 14.4). Stack the links that leave a bar in the order of the bars they reach, so none cross. Fold receivers of one kind into one bar with their count, by one rule for every side, and list each in the table. Draw two sides alike, side by side and in one ink, and name each side in words; money spent to elect a candidate takes one neutral ink for every party, with no red or blue (Rules 14.6 and 14.7).
use_when: The reader asks where money or influence went from a few senders, and which links carried the most.

use_instead.when: Money into one account and out of it
Many parts with many links among them
Links among items in a set order

text: Bars and links on one scale let a reader compare every sender and receiver of both sides at a glance, and names set beside the bars keep each end readable on a phone. Folding many small receivers keeps the drawing calm, and the table keeps every one. A rule that picks one sender for each side can make a contrast the record does not hold, so the drawing takes every sender the rule finds.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form network-diagram: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s73; encode source (the side each bar sends for), target, value, target_key and kind; labels.nodes folds rows into nodes by source and kind, labels.unit sets the measure one pixel of width carries, labels.key_steps the key, labels.ink the party-mark ink; draws its bars as tall as their dollars in the links’ unit, through K.parts.flows, flow_band and width_key.
